Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:


<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
`makepkg --printsrcinfo` only sources and evaluates the PKGBUILD's global/top-level scope. In this file, that scope contains exclusively standard, declarative AUR metadata: pkgname, pkgdesc, arch, url, license, depends/makedepends/optdepends/checkdepends arrays, provides, conflicts, source, b2sums (SKIP, which is standard for VCS sources and not a failure criterion), and options.

There is no executable code at the top level: no command substitutions that download or run payloads, no `eval`, no `curl`/`wget`, no obfuscation or encoding tricks, and no network activity. The `source` entry (`$_pkgname::git+$url.git`) merely declares that the package will be fetched from the project's own upstream GitHub repository — a normal VCS declaration, not an executable action.

The functions `pkgver()`, `prepare()`, `build()`, `check()`, and `package()` contain git/cargo operations and install commands, but these are inside function definitions and are never executed by `--printsrcinfo`; they are out of scope for this gate and will be audited in the full PKGBUILD review. The `pkgver()` function's git commands reference the declared upstream URL and use no remote override, so even a future full audit would show no indication of pulling from an unrelated host.

No security issues are present in the portion of the file that this command executes.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>Standard declarative PKGBUILD, no executable global code.</summary>
</security_assessment>

+ Initial PKGBUILD audit complete -- Standard declarative PKGBUILD, no executable global code.

<details>
The PKGBUILD contains only standard variable definitions and array assignments in its top-level (global) scope: `pkgname`, `_pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `url`, `license`, `depends`, `makedepends`, `optdepends`, `checkdepends`, `provides`, `conflicts`, `source`, `b2sums` (with `SKIP` for the VCS source, which is required and harmless), and `options`. There are no command substitutions, `eval` statements, network requests (curl/wget), base64 decoding, or file operations at the top level that could execute during `makepkg --printsrcinfo`.

The `source` array points to the package's own upstream repository (`https://github.com/FlowOSS/flowshot`) via git, which is the expected upstream source for this project. No code outside of `pkgver()`, `prepare()`, `build()`, or `package()` executes at this gate — and per the narrow scope of `--printsrcinfo`, those functions are out of scope anyway. Everything observed is consistent with ordinary AUR packaging practice.
</details>
<evidence>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is a clean, standard packaging script for a Rust application (flowshot, a Wayland/X11 screenshot tool). It only interacts with its declared upstream source (`https://github.com/FlowOSS/flowshot.git` via the `source` array) using `git`, and never performs `git pull`/`git fetch` with `--hard` resets in `prepare()` or `build()` — the mutable VCS source is fetched only through the declared `source` entry, so no unchecked content is pulled at build time.

All build steps are normal Rust packaging practices: `cargo fetch --locked`, `cargo build --release --frozen`, and `cargo test --frozen` — the `--frozen`/`--locked` flags actually strengthen supply-chain security by preventing unsanctioned dependency updates. There is no use of `eval`, `base64`, `curl`, `wget`, or any other command that downloads or executes code from an unexpected host. File operations are confined to installing built binaries, icons (generated locally from the SVG via `rsvg-convert`), man pages, completions, and license/docs files into `$pkgdir`.

No obfuscation, exfiltration, backdoors, credential theft, or modifications to unrelated system files are present. The `b2sums=SKIP` is expected and required for VCS sources, and is not a security concern.
</details>
